issues.description: Method name inconsistency: the example in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java calls farm.feed() (template Main.java, commented example line 20), but the problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 108-111) and the solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java, solution lines 27-31) use a method named feedAllAnimals(). A student who copies or uncomments the Main example will get a compilation error (no farm.feed() in the template/solution) and may be confused about which method to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template consistent with the UML/problem statement: update the commented example in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java to call farm.feedAllAnimals() instead of farm.feed(). (Alternative: add a delegating public void feed() method in the template Farm that calls feedAllAnimals(), but prefer updating the Main example to match the specification.)

issues.description: Concept: the Farm operation that triggers all animals to be fed. Problem statement and solution name the operation feedAllAnimals(), but the template's Main.java calls farm.feed(). Specifically: problem_statement.md and solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java define/implement a method named feedAllAnimals(), while template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java (commented example usage) invokes farm.feed(). A student following the template's example may search for or implement feed() (as shown in Main.java) instead of feedAllAnimals(), causing a mismatch between the specification and the starter code and increasing confusion when trying to run the provided Main example or to match tests that expect feedAllAnimals().
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template consistent with the specification and solution. Either (A) update the example call in template/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java to use farm.feedAllAnimals() instead of farm.feed(), or (B) add a feed() convenience method in Farm (template) that delegates to feedAllAnimals() (public void feed() { feedAllAnimals(); }) so the example in Main.java works while preserving the canonical name from the problem statement and solution.
